title: Pterostilbene Potentiates the NGF-TrkA Signaling Pathway, Enhancing Differentiation in PC12 Cells.
authors: Ospondpant, Dusadee; Gao, Xiong; Lin, Shengying; Ho, Yuen Man; Dong, Tina Ting Xia; Tsim, Karl Wah Keung
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
one_liner_zh: 该文研究紫檀芪增强NGF-TrkA信号促进PC12细胞分化，仅用分子对接验证小分子与NGF结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Pterostilbene, a stilbenoid found in vegetables and natural products, has therapeutic potential due to its multiple pharmacological actions. In the brain, the nerve growth factor (NGF) is a pivotal neurotrophic factor, serving for neuronal survival and differentiation. The decline in NGF levels in aged individuals contributes to the development of neurodegenerative processes and cognitive impairment. Here, we aim to explore the effect of pterostilbene on promoting neuron-like differentiation in PC12 cells, a well-established model to study neuronal differentiation, by potentiating the functions of NGF. Molecular docking and ultrafiltration assays were performed to examine the direct binding of pterostilbene with NGF. The mechanisms underlying the stimulation of PC12 cell differentiation, characterized by enhanced neurite outgrowth and increased neurofilament expression, were determined through TrkA/Akt/CREB signaling pathways. The combined treatment of pterostilbene with a low dose of NGF significantly potentiated the NGF-induced neurite extension and neurofilament expression. Pterostilbene enhanced the effect of NGF on promoting neuron-like differentiation, which was related to increased activation of the TrkA signaling pathway. This upstream event was associated with increased phosphorylation of Akt and CREB. The selective inhibitors of TrkA (K252a) and PI3K/Akt (LY294002) were applied to validate the NGF/TrkA/Akt signaling pathways leading to diminished neurite outgrowth and reduced expression of neurofilaments in cells treated with pterostilbene and NGF. Taken together, the results indicate that pterostilbene could potentiate NGF/TrkA activity, enhancing neuron-like differentiation in PC12 cells under a low concentration of NGF. These findings suggest that the application of pterostilbene could be a promising alternative therapeutic strategy to improve NGF efficacy.
abstract_zh: 紫檀芪（Pterostilbene）是一种存在于蔬菜和天然产物中的二苯乙烯类化合物，因其多种药理作用而具有治疗潜力。在大脑中，神经生长因子（NGF）是一种关键的神经营养因子，负责神经元的存活和分化。老年个体中NGF水平的下降与神经退行性过程和认知障碍的发展有关。在此，我们旨在探讨紫檀芪通过增强NGF功能，促进PC12细胞（一种研究神经元分化的成熟模型）神经元样分化的效果。采用分子对接和超滤实验检测紫檀芪与NGF的直接结合。通过TrkA/Akt/CREB信号通路，确定了PC12细胞分化刺激的机制，其特征为神经突生长增强和神经丝表达增加。紫檀芪与低剂量NGF的联合处理显著增强了NGF诱导的神经突延伸和神经丝表达。紫檀芪增强了NGF促进神经元样分化的效果，这与TrkA信号通路激活增加有关。这一上游事件与Akt和CREB磷酸化增加相关。应用TrkA（K252a）和PI3K/Akt（LY294002）的选择性抑制剂，验证了NGF/TrkA/Akt信号通路在紫檀芪和NGF处理的细胞中导致神经突生长减少和神经丝表达降低的作用。综上所述，结果表明紫檀芪能增强NGF/TrkA活性，在低浓度NGF条件下促进PC12细胞的神经元样分化。这些发现提示，紫檀芪的应用可能是一种改善NGF疗效的有前景的替代治疗策略。
